description: The date line, the subject line, and the default greeting and sign-off of a cover letter appear in the letter's own language. The editor preview, the PDF and the Word export all show the same wording.

userStories.title: The exports show the date, subject and defaults in the letter's language
userStories.description: As a user downloading a French, German or Italian cover letter, I want its date and subject line in that language, so that the letter does not mix languages.
acceptanceCriteria: For a letter whose text is detected as French, the PDF and the Word file show: the date in French format, e.g. "2 novembre 2026"; the subject "Objet : Candidature au poste de <job title>"; when greeting or sign-off is empty, the French defaults "Madame, Monsieur," and "Veuillez agréer mes salutations distinguées,".

The same holds for German (e.g. "2. November 2026", "Betreff: Bewerbung als <job title>", "Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren," / "Mit freundlichen Grüßen,") and Italian (e.g. "2 novembre 2026", "Oggetto: Candidatura per la posizione di <job title>", "Gentili Signore e Signori," / "Cordiali saluti,").
An English letter keeps today's wording exactly: "November 2, 2026", "Re: Application for <job title>", "Dear Hiring Manager,", "Sincerely,".
When the language cannot be detected, the page language is used. The PDF and Word routes know it from the request's locale.
A non-empty stored greeting or sign-off is printed as stored, in any language.
The PDF and the Word file of the same letter show identical text for these four parts.

FR-1: One resolver decides the display language of a letter. Input: its opening, body and closing text with the markup removed. Detection: through the existing `detectOfferLanguage`. Fallback: the page or request locale. The preview, the PDF and the Word file all use this resolver.

FR-2: Wording per language lives in the existing i18n locale files, or in one shared constant set, with one entry per language. The date uses `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with the resolved locale (`fr-CH`/`de-CH`/`it-CH` or `fr-FR`/`de-DE`/`it-IT`, chosen once and documented) in long format.
FR-3: `coverLetterParts()` stays the single source of parts, order and defaults. The preview template consumes it, or the same helpers, instead of its own copies.
FR-4: No schema migration, no new dependency, no change to stored data.
FR-5: New strings exist in fr, en, de and it (`src/locales/locale-parity.test.ts`).
Regression constraint: The English output of the PDF and Word export is byte-identical for these parts to today's ("Re: Application for …", "Dear Hiring Manager,", "Sincerely,", en-US date).

Regression constraint: Every other part of the PDF and Word output is unchanged, and so are their layout, page size and paging. The specs `e2e/cover-letter-pdf-export.spec.ts` and `e2e/cover-letter-docx-export.spec.ts` stay green, with only expected-text updates where a test fixture is non-English.
Regression constraint: The preview's layout and the editor's other behaviour are unchanged (`e2e/cover-letter-editor-i18n.spec.ts`, `e2e/cover-letter-editor-spacing.spec.ts`).
Regression constraint: The translate-by-flag copies and cover-letter-from-job letters are unchanged in what they store.
Regression constraint: Resume exports and parity are unchanged (NEW 0 / KNOWN 3).
Verification: The `CLAUDE.md` §14 baseline, plus `pnpm test:parity`.

Verification: Unit tests: the resolver: fr/en/de/it detected, undetectable text falling back to the locale, markup ignored; the wording and date for each language; `coverLetterParts()` in each language; English output pinned to today's text.

Verification: e2e: preview, PDF and Word for a French letter opened under `/de` and a German letter opened under `/fr`: the four parts follow the letter; an undetectable short letter follows the page; an English letter is unchanged.
Verification: `export-validation`: PDF and Word for fr, de and it letters. Extracted text shows the localized parts, and PDF and Word agree.
Verification: `ui-expert` on the preview in fr and de at 1440 and 375.
Verification: `code-reviewer`.
FAIL condition: A letter detected as fr, de or it shows an English date, subject or default formula in the preview, the PDF or the Word file.
FAIL condition: The preview, the PDF and the Word file disagree on any of the four parts for the same letter.
FAIL condition: English output changes.
FAIL condition: A stored greeting or sign-off is replaced by a default.
FAIL condition: A second copy of the date, subject or default rules remains in the template.
BLOCKER condition: Detecting the language reliably on typical letter text needs a new dependency or a schema change. Report it; the owner decides.
Out of scope: Storing a language column, or letting the user choose the letter's language.
Out of scope: Translating the letter's own text, recipient, title or any stored value.
Out of scope: Changing the greeting and sign-off values that creation flows store in the database (e.g. "Dear Hiring Manager," written by the form without an application).
Out of scope: Template layout, fonts and spacing.
Out of scope: The editor header overflow at 375 (draft PRD `cover-letter-editor-responsive`).
Out of scope: The public cover-letter generator tool.

userStories.title: The editor preview shows exactly what the exports show
userStories.description: As a user editing a cover letter, I want the preview's date, subject and default formulas to be the ones I will download, so that what I see is what I get.
acceptanceCriteria: The editor preview takes the date, the subject and the default greeting and sign-off from the same parts and formatting as the PDF and Word exports. No second copy of these rules exists in the template.
For the same letter and page, the preview's text for these four parts equals the PDF's text.
Changing the letter's paragraphs to another language updates the preview's date, subject and defaults once the language is detected. The preview follows the current editor content, saved or not.
Apart from these four parts, the preview looks the same as before: same layout, fonts, spacing and section order.
